sections.skill: Use odd/even and alternation to predict outcomes and rule out possibilities

questions.prompt: Gears that touch mesh: when one turns clockwise, a gear touching it turns counterclockwise, and the reverse. Seven gears form a closed ring, each touching the gears on either side (figure). Gear 1 is turned clockwise. What happens?

choices.text: Every gear turns, and the directions alternate around the ring.
The gears jam: going around the ring, gear 1 would have to turn both ways.

questions.correct_answer: The gears jam: going around the ring, gear 1 would have to turn both ways.

figure.description: A closed ring of 7 numbered gears, each touching the gears on either side.

questions.prompt: Gears that touch mesh: when one turns clockwise, a gear touching it turns counterclockwise, and the reverse. Twelve gears stand in a row (not a ring), each touching the next. Gear 1 turns clockwise. How many of the 12 gears turn counterclockwise?
A frog starts on 0 on a number line and makes exactly 9 jumps, each 1 unit left or right. It can end on 4.
A lamp starts OFF. Each press of its switch changes it (OFF to ON, or ON to OFF). Give a number of presses from 1 to 20 that leaves the lamp ON.
questions.rule: isInteger(n) and n >= 1 and n <= 20 and isOdd(n)
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: isInteger(n) and n >= 1 and n <= 20 and isOdd(n) (example: n = 7)

questions.prompt: A token moves along a row of squares numbered 1 to 15. Each move jumps exactly 2 squares left or right (staying on the row). It starts on square 4. How many of the 15 squares can it ever reach, counting square 4?

sections.skill: Strategy: keep track of odd and even only
sections.relationship: Students follow every step of a long process. Often only odd/even matters, and it switches or stays the same at each step.
sections.author_note: Students follow every step of a long process. Often only odd/even matters, and it switches or stays the same at each step.

lesson.title: Keep track of odd and even only
text: Ask what happens to odd/even at each step. Does it switch every time, or stay the same?
If it switches every step, after an even number of steps it is back where it began; after an odd number it is the other way.
A target with the wrong parity can never be reached, however the steps are chosen.

example.title: Worked example (a different puzzle)
prompt: A card shows its red side. Each turn it is flipped over. After 25 turns, which side shows?
steps: Each flip switches the side. After an even number of flips it shows red again.
25 is odd, so after 25 flips the other side shows.

questions.prompt: The sum of 5 odd numbers is odd.
A coin starts heads up. It is turned over 13 times. Which side is up at the end?

choices.text: Either side, depending on how it is turned
It cannot be known without trying

questions.prompt: Gears that touch mesh: when one turns clockwise, a gear touching it turns counterclockwise, and the reverse. Nine gears stand in a row, each touching the next. Gear 1 turns clockwise. What is the number of the last gear in the row that turns clockwise?
An even number plus an odd number is even.
Which total CANNOT be the sum of three odd numbers?

sections.relationship: Harder: parity on grids, rings and sign choices.
sections.label: ADVANCED APPLICATION

questions.prompt: A token starts on a corner square of a 5 by 5 board. Each move goes to a square sharing a side (going back is allowed). After exactly 7 moves, how many different squares could the token be on?
Gears that touch mesh: when one turns clockwise, a gear touching it turns counterclockwise, and the reverse. Ten gears form a closed ring, each touching the gears on either side. They can all turn.
Seven cups stand upside down. A move turns over exactly 4 cups (any 4). Can all seven cups end right side up?

choices.text: No: each move changes the number of upside-down cups by an even amount, so it stays odd.
Yes: turn over 4 cups, then 3 cups.
No: 7 is not a multiple of 4.

questions.correct_answer: No: each move changes the number of upside-down cups by an even amount, so it stays odd.

questions.prompt: Put a + or - sign in front of each of the numbers 1, 2, 3, ..., 10 and add. Give a total from 0 to 10 that can be made this way.
questions.rule: isInteger(t) and t >= 0 and t <= 10 and isOdd(t)
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: isInteger(t) and t >= 0 and t <= 10 and isOdd(t) (example: t = 1)

questions.prompt: Gears that touch mesh: when one turns clockwise, a gear touching it turns counterclockwise, and the reverse. Nine gears are arranged in a 3 by 3 square, and each gear touches the gears directly beside, above and below it. A corner gear turns clockwise. How many gears turn clockwise, including the corner gear?

sections.relationship: Expert: parity arguments about paths and totals.
sections.label: EXPERT CHALLENGE

questions.prompt: A token must visit every square of a 5 by 5 board exactly once, each move going to a square that shares a side. It starts on the square next to a corner (row 1, column 2). Is this possible?

choices.text: Yes, but only if it ends on a corner.
Yes: go along row 1, then snake back and forth.
No: 25 is not a multiple of 5.
No: the path must start and end on the corner color, and this square has the other color.

questions.correct_answer: No: the path must start and end on the corner color, and this square has the other color.

questions.prompt: Put a + or - sign in front of each of the numbers 1, 2, 3, ..., 10 and add. How many different totals can be made?
On a square grid, a path that moves one square up, down, left or right at each step, and ends where it started, always has an even number of steps.

Gears that touch mesh: when one turns clockwise, a gear touching it turns counterclockwise, and the reverse. Give a number of gears n from 3 to 12 for which a closed ring of n gears, each touching its two neighbors, would jam.
questions.rule: isInteger(n) and n >= 3 and n <= 12 and isOdd(n)
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: isInteger(n) and n >= 3 and n <= 12 and isOdd(n) (example: n = 5)
